Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple, well-defined pulmonary nodules of varying sizes (some up to 3 cm) that are predominantly located in the lower lung zones without evidence of calcification. This specific radiographic pattern, combined with the negative tuberculin reaction and clinical history, supports the diagnosis of necrotizing sarcoid granulomatosis over tuberculosis or typical sarcoidosis which usually favor upper zones.
